title: Henry Lambert and the early country bands
summary: Allen asks about Henry Lambert. Ridgley says he played tuba and bass with him in the string band in Jefferson and earlier in military bands.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Did you know a fellow named Henry Lambert way back?

Yeah, Henry Lambert. He lives out in Jefferson. That's the man played with us when we started our band up there and Professor Humperty was teaching I told you he played a, he was a tuba player, he played on, and then he played bass, violin, and the band up there on trombone. Well that was the old man Lambert, but they got a Lambert up there now, still living in Jefferson Pires, his son. But the old man played with us. He used to play the tuba.
I don't think. No. I mean, but Lambert played. Well how did you get his name?
From the year before, when Russell talked to you before. Well I'm listening to it, I want to ask you about him, you know who he played with?

The Lambert? Yeah. He played with me, then after he stopped playing with me, he set up a little band of his own up there when I left, coming to New Orleans. But long before that he used to play in all those military bands, like Fumes and things, old man, Joy Moret and all those people back there. He played with them. But when he got into the string band he played up there with me.
He would play with the Excelsior and the Orwood and the ...
Yeah. Played with all of them.
All those old, little town grass bands.
